purpose: Remove the openai_api_key/anthropic_api_key/gemini_api_key inputs from the reusable review/audit/autofix workflows so API keys can only be supplied via GitHub Secrets, and add a shared composite action that emits soft ::warning:: annotations when the selected model needs an unconfigured key.
riskRationale: The security goal (keys only via secrets) and all prior review feedback (env binding, de-duplication, migration docs, heuristic scope) are correctly implemented and verified. However, the new composite action is referenced with a workspace-relative path (uses: ./.github/actions/validate-api-keys) inside reusable workflows, and GitHub resolves ./-relative action references against the caller's checked-out workspace, so the validation step will hard-fail every cross-repo consumer of review.yml, audit.yml, and autofix.yml — the documented primary use case of these public workflows.
breakingChanges: Removed openai_api_key/anthropic_api_key/gemini_api_key workflow_call.inputs from review.yml, audit.yml, and autofix.yml — callers must now supply OPENAI_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY via secrets: inherit or an explicit secrets: mapping, otherwise the workflow call fails validation with 'Unexpected input(s)'

The new relative-path composite action reference (./.github/actions/validate-api-keys) breaks cross-repo callers of all three reusable workflows at the 'Validate API key secrets' step until it is changed to a fully-qualified owner/repo path (e.g. nilesh32236/opencode-ai-reviewer/.github/actions/validate-api-keys@v1) or the $/ self-repository syntax

text: The core fix is correct and complete: API keys are now accepted exclusively via secrets, the four copy-pasted validation blocks were consolidated into a clean composite action that never interpolates the model into shell, and the breaking input removal is documented in the README and every workflow header. However, the new composite action is referenced via a workspace-relative path that resolves against the caller's repository, so the Validate API key secrets step will fail for every cross-repo consumer of the three reusable workflows. Two minor non-blocking notes (secret-passing hygiene and a quick-start doc gap) round out the review.

reasoning: The security intent and all prior review feedback are properly implemented, but the newly introduced uses: ./.github/actions/validate-api-keys relative reference cannot resolve when the reusable workflows are invoked from another repository (their documented primary use), causing the validation step to hard-fail every external caller until it is switched to a fully-qualified owner/repo reference or the $/ self-repository syntax.

message: Binding the model through the step env (MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}) and referencing $MODEL in the script cleanly eliminates the ${{ inputs.model }} shell-interpolation vector that was previously flagged; grep confirms no inputs.* model value is spliced into any run: script anymore.

The explicit breaking-change migration callout plus the per-workflow header notes (review.yml:18 and equivalents in audit.yml and autofix.yml) clearly tell existing callers that with:-passed keys now hard-fail validation and how to migrate to secrets: inherit or an explicit secrets: mapping — directly addressing the previously reported communication gap.

Extracting the four copy-pasted validation blocks into one composite action referenced from all four jobs is the right de-duplication move; the header honestly documents that provider detection is heuristic (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini only), and soft ::warning:: annotations that never fail, with a no-op default for the standard OpenCode model, are the right behavior for a public reusable workflow.

uses: ./.github/actions/validate-api-keys uses a workspace-relative path inside reusable workflows (same reference at audit.yml:91 and autofix.yml:88,120). Reusable workflows execute in the caller's repository context, and GitHub resolves ./-relative action references against the checked-out workspace — the checkout step fetches the CALLER's repo, which does not contain this composite action. Every external consumer of these public reusable workflows (README Option A documents uses: nilesh32236/opencode-ai-reviewer/.github/workflows/review.yml@v1) will fail the new step with 'Can't find action.yml/action.yaml under .../.github/actions/validate-api-keys' and the whole job aborts, breaking the feature for exactly the cross-repo audience it exists for.
suggestion: Reference the composite action with the same fully-qualified owner/repo form already used for the main action in these files, applied to all four call sites (review.yml, audit.yml, autofix.yml x2) and versioned together with the workflows so a @v1 tag resolves it; alternatively use the new self-repository syntax (uses: $/.github/actions/validate-api-keys) which resolves to the workflow's own repository at the running commit and needs no checkout.
suggestionCode:
- name: Validate API key secrets
        uses: nilesh32236/opencode-ai-reviewer/.github/actions/validate-api-keys@v1

message: The composite action receives the three API key secrets via with: inputs (review.yml:110-112, audit.yml:94-96, autofix.yml:91-93 and 123-125). GitHub's hardening guidance recommends passing secrets to composite actions through env rather than inputs, since input values are rendered into the step context and can surface in logs if the action ever echoes them. In practice GitHub masks these values and the composite only tests for non-emptiness, so the actual risk is low, but for a secrets-focused security fix it is the one remaining anti-pattern.
suggestion: Declare OPENAI_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY at job level via env: (env values propagate into composite action steps) and have the composite action read ${{ env.OPENAI_API_KEY }} instead of inputs, keeping the keys out of the action's input context.

message: The quick-start example (lines 34-38) and the claim 'the GitHub Token is auto-inherited via secrets: inherit' are inconsistent with the workflows' actual contract: review.yml/audit.yml/autofix.yml all read ${{ secrets.repo_token }} (a required workflow_call secret), and secrets: inherit only forwards secrets by their literal name — it does not forward GITHUB_TOKEN under the name repo_token. A new user following the quick start will end up with an empty github_token input and a failing action unless they also create a repository secret literally named repo_token. Since this PR rewrites the secrets guidance in this exact section, it should clarify that repo_token must be a PAT (or mapped secret) in the caller repo.
suggestion: In the new secrets-configuration note, add that secrets: inherit forwards the caller's secrets by name, so the caller must define a repo_token secret (a PAT with the documented permissions, or map GITHUB_TOKEN explicitly via a secrets: mapping) for the shipped workflows to authenticate.
